assessment: O-02-5 uses PD for pancreaticoduodenectomy and estimates perioperative energy requirements.

O-03-2 reports rigidity and akinesia after short-bowel surgery in stage IV Parkinson disease. Multiple candidate explanations include drug interruption, haloperidol, absorption and amino acid changes.
O-05-1 uses PD for pancreaticoduodenectomy in a postoperative quality of life comparison.
O-13-3 uses PD for progressive disease after nivolumab in gastric cancer. The adjacent report concerns feeding access after esophageal cancer surgery.
O-16-2 concerns anti-PD-1 antibody therapy in gastric cancer. O-16-3 tests EPA with cisplatin in esophageal cancer cells.
O-24-3 mentions Parkinson bowel dysfunction in discussion. Tube-feeding ward results after monitoring and bowel medication adjustment were pooled across 25 patients.
O-31-3 uses PD for progressive disease after preoperative chemotherapy for esophageal cancer.
O-41-3 uses Pd for palladium in hair elemental analysis. Potato material on the page is dextrin in enteral formula.

O-48-4 compares tube-delivered water temperatures and stool consistency in four Parkinson patients. Kale is a substring of the Japanese word for scale and shiso comes from adjacent words in O-48-5. Neither ingredient was administered.
O-49-1 reports concurrent oral intake after PEG for 46% of 13 Parkinson patients among 33 neurologic cases. No specific foods or food-level outcomes.
O-55-3 uses PD for peritoneal dialysis in a gastrostomy case with dysphagia after chemoradiotherapy.
O-56-3 is the original 91-person outpatient CONUT study later reproduced by the authors' institute. No food exposure was estimated.
O-73-3 uses PD for pancreaticoduodenectomy in a postoperative nutrition and body-composition analysis.
O-80-3 compared body composition and markers in 59 patients by BMI. The report gives no diet intake or longitudinal weight-change data.
O-99-1 reports neck interferential current stimulation in three Parkinson cases. Liquid videofluoroscopy and inhaled citric acid assessed airway and cough outcomes.
O-99-2 groups patients by prescription, including anti-Parkinson drugs, and compares dysphagia with drug combinations. The second abstract is a stroke cohort.

O-101-6 records oral jelly trials and later paste-texture meals in newly diagnosed Parkinson disease with several comorbidities and PEG complications. Neither food identity nor a food-specific aspiration result was established.
O-103-5 counts anti-Parkinson drug use among 52 patients with paralytic ileus at a psychiatric hospital and gives pooled outcomes after bowel rest and medication review.
